newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks firm 0.59pct, focus on blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks firm 0.59pct, focus on blue chips.

text.p: Greek shares rose 0.59 percent clearing 1,600 points on Monday helped by upbeat industrial and banking stocks and brokers said blue chips were taking centre stage again.

"We are witnessing a return of trading interest in blue chips, especially those which produce headlines for their corporate action and expected interim profitability," said Lambros Papakonstantinou, managing director of P&K Securities.
"This means that price imbalances between blue chips and second-tier stocks developed during this year's rally are accentuated," he added.
The Athens general index settled just clear of 1,600 points, adding 0.59 percent or 9.46 points to 1,600.90 from Friday's 1,591.44 close.
Buying interest in blue chips was outweighed by supply on the same stocks at their intra-day highs.

"Today we saw increased supply in blue chips such as National Bank, OTE telecom and Titan Cement at their intra-day highs," said Papakonstantinou. "There seems to be strong buying interest at lower price levels although many investors are sidelined," he added.
The market was seen consolidating its gains around 1,600 points following the recent 150 point rebound.
"Current trading is mostly linked to cherry picking rather than across-the-board buying," he said.
